description:
Estou participando do desafio Construa um Treinador de Missão para Astronautas Juniores. Quero criar um jogo educativo em que os jogadores tomem decisões para manter uma base lunar funcionando. Tenho interesse em espaço, tecnologia e ideias criativas. Vou me dedicar para ajudar em todas as etapas, da ideia à apresentação. Busco pessoas colaborativas que curtam programação, design, jogos, pesquisa ou comunicação — não precisa saber fazer tudo!

details:
Alfonsi Mission is a single-player space training simulator for learners aged 8 and older. Players choose an age group—8–10, 11–13, 14–17, or 18+—and progress through learning levels suited to their experience. They begin with activities on Earth, such as interpreting satellite images and space data, then advance to a first-person 3D space station. A mission commander introduces tasks as players explore station modules, learn how systems work, and make decisions about power, water, air, food, radiation protection, and maintenance. The experience includes lessons, calculations, practical challenges, 3D equipment analysis, workshop activities, spacewalk simulations, free exploration, and progress tracking. The planned campaign spans 30 mission days. Players who meet the learning requirements can earn an educational certificate; it is not a professional qualification or an official NASA certificate.

What benefits does it offer?
The game connects scientific concepts to mission decisions. Players investigate, calculate, choose between options, and see the consequences in the simulation. Content is adapted to different age groups and offered in multiple languages, with accessibility options and explanations in different formats. External videos supplement the lessons, with written explanations available as an alternative.

What impact does the project aim to have?
Alfonsi Mission aims to make space science more approachable and engaging, especially for learners who find lecture-based lessons difficult or are unsure where to begin. It introduces astronomy, physics, Earth and space science, and mission systems through active learning.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software were used?
The project is a browser-based web application built with TypeScript, compiled to JavaScript. It uses React for the interface and game state, Three.js with WebGL for first-person 3D rendering, Tailwind CSS for styling, and Vite for development and bundling. The interface uses HTML5 and CSS3 and runs on compatible devices with a web browser; no specialized space hardware is required. Google AI Studio was used during development.

What is creative about the project?
It combines age-adapted learning paths, first-person 3D exploration, and mission-system management in one learning journey. Historical NASA space-weather events, including DONKI records, inspire in-game scenarios. The project distinguishes observed data from educational simplifications and does not present the simulation as a forecast or real operational procedure.

What factors did the team consider?
The project considered learners’ ages and prior knowledge, clear explanations, accessibility, multiple languages, scientific accuracy, device compatibility, and the distinction between educational simulation and professional astronaut training. It also aims to keep the experience engaging through mission goals, practical decisions, visible consequences, and progress toward a completion certificate.
